title: Topic Drill: Reading Informational Texts (Set A)

items.stem:
Notice from the Pellam Canal Trust: Beginning in March, volunteers will restore the long-closed Dray Lane lock, which has sat dry since the mill shut down. Work crews will clear silt, replace two rotted gates, and rebuild the stone steps along the towpath. Visitors may watch from the footbridge on Saturdays, but the lock area will be fenced during weekdays. The Trust expects boats to pass through by autumn if the weather allows work to continue on schedule.

What is the main idea of the notice?
options: The closing of the mill has caused the whole canal to be fenced off from the public for good
Boats will be banned from the canal until the autumn
Weekday visitors must pay to cross the footbridge
Volunteers will restore a closed lock, and the public may watch on Saturdays
items.explanation: The notice announces that volunteers will restore the Dray Lane lock from March and that visitors may watch on Saturdays, which together make the main idea. The mill closing is only background, not a cause of permanent fencing. Boats are expected to pass through by autumn, not banned, and no fee for the footbridge is mentioned.

items.stem:
Field report, Pellam Canal, Week 6. The dredge removed about 40 cubic yards of silt from the basin above the lock, far less than the 90 planned, because a buried iron chain jammed the bucket twice. Crew leader Dana Ruiz decided to pause dredging and use the delay to inspect the stone walls, where she found three cracked blocks. Replacement stone is on order. Dredging will resume once the chain is cut free and hauled away.

According to the report, why did the dredge remove less silt than planned?
options: Replacement stone arrived too late for the crew to continue
Three wall blocks collapsed into the basin and blocked the dredge
A buried chain jammed the bucket twice
Dana Ruiz lowered the target after inspecting the walls
items.explanation: The report says the dredge took out about 40 yards instead of 90 because a buried iron chain jammed the bucket twice. The stone is still on order, so it cannot have arrived late. The three blocks were cracked, not collapsed, and the inspection happened because of the pause, not before it as a reason for a lower target.

items.stem:
To the Editor: I walked the Pellam towpath last Sunday and counted eleven strollers, four cyclists, and a family fishing with paper cups tied to string. Ten years ago the same stretch held broken glass and tall weeds, and I rarely met anyone. Restoring the old lock will cost money, certainly, but I suspect the towpath has already paid back a portion of what it was given. I urge neighbors to attend the March meeting and ask where the next dollar should go.

Which inference is best supported by the letter?
options: The writer believes earlier spending on the towpath has brought real benefit
The writer opposes the lock project because the cost seems far too high for the neighbors
The towpath is still unsafe and empty on most days
The March meeting has been cancelled for lack of interest
items.explanation: The writer contrasts today’s busy path with the broken glass and weeds of ten years ago and says it has paid back a portion of what it was given, so the writer sees benefit from past spending. The letter admits the cost but does not oppose the project. The path is busy now, and the meeting is encouraged, not cancelled.

items.stem:
A canal lock lifts boats without any engine on the bank. A boat enters a sealed chamber, and the gates behind it close. Then valves open in the upper gate, and water flows in until the chamber matches the higher level. The front gates swing open, and the boat motors out onto the upper stretch. Lowering a boat reverses the steps: the valves drain the chamber until it matches the lower level. Only gravity moves the water.

The author most likely wrote this passage to do what?
options: Persuade readers to volunteer their weekends at a lock near them
Explain how a lock moves boats between water levels
Entertain readers with the story of a canal trip
Argue that engines should be banned from canals
items.explanation: The passage walks through each step of raising and lowering a boat and ends with the fact that only gravity moves the water, which shows an aim to explain a process. It never asks readers to volunteer, so it is not persuasion. It tells no story of a trip, and it never takes a position on engines.

items.stem:
The restoration unfolds in three phases. First, crews drain the damaged section and survey its walls. Next, masons rebuild the failed stonework and pour a new clay lining to hold water. Finally, the section is refilled slowly over ten days so the new lining can settle without cracking. Each phase must finish before the next begins, since refilling too early would wash out the fresh clay.

How is the passage mainly organized?
options: By comparing two methods of restoring a canal wall
By stating a problem and listing several rejected solutions
As a sequence of steps, each depending on the one before
By describing the canal from its east end to its west end
items.explanation: The words first, next and finally, along with the statement that each phase must finish before the next begins, mark a sequence in which steps depend on one another. Only one method is described, so there is no comparison. No solutions are rejected, and nothing in the passage moves along the canal from one end to the other.

items.stem:
Marguerite Oyelaran has driven the county bookmobile for nine years, and her shelves hold a surprising range: seed catalogs, large-print mysteries, repair manuals, and picture books worn soft at the corners. Because the roads past Tillow Ridge wash out each spring, she keeps a hand-drawn map of back routes tucked above the sun visor. Regular borrowers say she remembers what each household likes to read before they say a word.

As used in the passage, the word range most nearly means which of the following?
options: distance
variety
limit
mountain chain
items.explanation: The sentence lists seed catalogs, mysteries, manuals and picture books, so the shelves hold a variety of material. Distance is another common meaning but nothing is measured here. Limit is wrong because the list shows breadth, not a boundary, and mountain chain borrows a meaning that has no connection to the books on her shelves.

items.stem:
After the county cut the bookmobile’s weekday stops from six to four, borrowing at the Ferrin Mill stop fell by a third, and the Orchard Row stop, which kept its Tuesday visit, grew by a fifth. The librarians studied the sign-in sheets and learned that Mill families who lost their stop did not drive to the branch library, which is eleven miles away. They simply stopped borrowing.

According to the report, what resulted from cutting the Ferrin Mill stop?
options: Families there drove the eleven miles to the branch library to keep borrowing
Families at Orchard Row stopped borrowing altogether
The county restored all six weekday stops
Families there borrowed far less instead of traveling to the branch
items.explanation: The report says borrowing at Ferrin Mill fell by a third and that families did not drive the eleven miles to the branch, they simply stopped borrowing. The branch trip is directly denied. Orchard Row grew by a fifth rather than stopping, and nothing says the county restored its six stops.

items.stem:
Text 1: The bookmobile is a lifeline for rural readers. Without it, families on Tillow Ridge would travel eleven miles for a single picture book, and many simply would not go. Text 2: A bookmobile is charming, but a van with two thousand titles cannot match a branch with forty thousand. The county should spend its money on digital lending, which reaches every home at once.

Which statement best describes how the two texts differ?
options: Text 1 stresses access for remote families, while Text 2 favors a wider collection delivered digitally
Text 1 criticizes the van’s high operating cost, while Text 2 praises the van for reaching rural readers
Both texts argue that the branch library should close
Text 1 describes digital lending, while Text 2 describes the ridge
items.explanation: Text 1 focuses on remote families who would not travel eleven miles, and Text 2 points to the van’s small collection and recommends digital lending. Neither text criticizes cost in the way described, since Text 2 only suggests where money should go. Neither calls for closing the branch, and the ridge and digital lending are not swapped between them.

items.stem:
I expected a cramped, forgettable half hour. Instead, Mr. Abara folded himself into a child-sized chair aboard the Linden Vale bookmobile, handed out paper bird masks, and read about a heron with such comic dread that even the restless six-year-olds in the back stopped fidgeting. By the end, parents were laughing as loudly as the children. If the van has a flaw, it is only that the story hour ends too soon.

Which word best describes the tone of the review?
options: Coldly and harshly critical
Anxiously and fearfully uncertain
Warmly appreciative
Mockingly and bitterly sarcastic
items.explanation: The reviewer admits low expectations, then praises the chair, the masks, the comic reading and the laughing parents, and names only one flaw, that the hour ends too soon. That is warm appreciation. Cold criticism ignores the praise, anxiety is never shown, and sarcasm would mean saying the opposite of what is meant.

items.stem:
Notice: Starting in June, the Linden Vale bookmobile adds a wheelchair lift and a low shelf of large-print titles. Staff will carry requested books to riders’ doors at the Pine Court senior apartments every second Friday. Library cards can be renewed aboard the van without a fee. All stops remain on the posted schedule, although hours may shift during storms.

Which detail best shows that the van is making borrowing possible for people who cannot easily climb steps?
options: Library cards can be renewed aboard the van without a fee
Hours may shift during storms
All stops remain on the posted schedule
The van is adding a wheelchair lift
items.explanation: A wheelchair lift lets a person who cannot climb steps board the van, so it directly supports the claim. Free card renewal concerns cost, not access to the doorway. Storm-related hours and a steady posted schedule describe timing, and neither one helps a rider who cannot manage steps.

items.stem:
At the Corbin Creek hatchery, trout begin life as eggs in shallow trays through which cold water flows constantly. After about a month the eggs hatch into alevins that live off a yolk sac and stay hidden in the gravel-lined trays. Once the sac is absorbed, the young fish, now called fry, are moved to outdoor tanks and fed small pellets. Staff grade them by size weekly so larger fish do not crowd out smaller ones.

What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Cold running water is the only factor that decides whether young trout survive at the hatchery
Hatchery trout pass through stages that call for different housing and care
Hatchery staff sort fish so that the largest can be sold
Trout hatch faster in outdoor tanks than in trays
items.explanation: The passage follows trout from eggs in trays to alevins in gravel to fry in outdoor tanks, each stage with its own housing and feeding. That makes stages and care the main idea. Cold water is mentioned only for the eggs, selling fish is never discussed, and the passage never compares hatching speed in tanks with trays.

items.stem:
Memo to staff: Please log the water temperature at both intake pipes every morning and again at dusk. Last week, the reading at the north pipe climbed four degrees in under an hour, and without the evening entry we would not have noticed that the shade cloth had slipped. A late log would have cost us the whole tank. If the reading rises above the red line on the chart, call Ewan first and move the fish second.

What can be inferred about why the evening entry matters?
options: It can reveal a sudden problem before the fish are harmed
Staff often forget to record the morning readings at the north intake pipe
The red line on the chart was changed last week
The shade cloth is replaced every evening
items.explanation: The memo says the evening entry exposed a slipped shade cloth and a four degree climb, and that a late log could have cost a whole tank, so the entry helps catch trouble early. Nothing says the morning readings are forgotten, the chart line is described only as a limit, and the cloth had slipped by accident rather than being replaced.

items.stem:
A fish ladder is a series of low pools that lets migrating fish climb past a dam. Each step raises the water only a short distance, so even a tired salmon can leap or swim to the next pool and rest. Engineers watch the flow closely: too gentle, and fish may not find the entrance; too forceful, and they exhaust themselves. At the Wren Falls hatchery, a counting window lets visitors tally the fish as they pass.

As used in the passage, the word exhaust most nearly means which of the following?
options: release from a holding pen
drain of water
tire out completely
puff out smoke
items.explanation: The sentence warns that a flow too forceful would affect fish that already struggle to climb, so exhaust means tire out completely. Let escape confuses it with release, drain of water belongs to an emptied container, and puff out smoke borrows the engine meaning, which does not make sense for fish.

items.stem:
Dear friends of the Corbin Creek hatchery: Last spring a late freeze threatened half our eggs. Thanks to your gifts, we installed a backup pump in time, and 41,000 fingerlings were released into the river in June. Another freeze may come. The pump needs a second generator, which costs $2,400, and we are asking you to help us reach that figure by September.

What is the main purpose of the letter?
options: To warn readers about a late freeze that has already ended this year
To thank donors and request support toward a specific need
To explain how pumps move water through the hatchery
To announce the date of the June release
items.explanation: The letter thanks donors for the pump, then asks for help reaching $2,400 by September, so its purpose is thanks plus a specific request. The freeze is mentioned as background, not the point. No explanation of pumps is given, and the June release is recalled as a past result rather than announced.

items.stem:
In midsummer the rearing ponds at the hatchery turned murky green. Tests showed that warm weather and runoff from a nearby field had fed a bloom of algae, which was using up oxygen at night. Staff added aerators and shaded the ponds with netting, and within a week the water cleared and the fish stopped gathering at the surface.

How is the passage mainly organized?
options: Two ponds are compared point by point
Events are told in order from hatching to release
A claim about algae is stated and then argued against by two different experts
A problem is described, its causes are found, and a solution follows
items.explanation: The passage opens with green ponds, names warm weather and runoff as causes, and ends with aerators, netting and clearer water, which is problem, cause and solution. It never sets two ponds side by side. It does not follow fish from hatching to release, and no claim is raised and then rebutted.

items.stem:
Tamsin Ardeel runs the Hollow Creek seed bank from a converted dairy barn. Inside, glass jars of beans, squash and flax stand in rows, each labeled with the grower’s name and the year of collection. Tamsin tests a sample from every jar once a year by sprouting twenty seeds on damp paper. If fewer than fifteen sprout, she asks a local gardener to grow the variety out and return fresh seed.

According to the passage, what does Tamsin do when fewer than fifteen of the twenty seeds sprout?
options: She asks a gardener to grow the variety and return fresh seed
She discards the whole jar and then removes the label from its shelf
She tests another twenty seeds the same day
She moves the jar to a cooler end of the barn
items.explanation: The passage states that if fewer than fifteen sprout, Tamsin asks a local gardener to grow the variety and return fresh seed. Throwing out the jar, retesting on the same day and moving the jar to a cooler spot are all plausible habits for a seed keeper, but none of them appears in the text.

items.stem:
Seeds keep longest when they are dry, cool and sealed. A seed bank first dries each sample until it feels brittle, then seals it in a foil pouch and stores it at about the temperature of a household freezer. Low moisture slows the chemical changes that eventually make seeds unable to sprout, and low temperature slows them further. Under such conditions, some grains stay viable for decades, while the same grains left on a warm shelf might last only a few years.

Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?
options: Foil pouches are the only reliable way to store any kind of grain for many years
Household freezers work better than seed bank storage
Seeds always last for decades once they are dried
Dryness and cold slow the changes that make seeds lose the ability to sprout
items.explanation: The passage explains that low moisture and low temperature slow the chemical changes that end a seed’s ability to sprout. Foil pouches are one step, not the only method. Freezer temperature is only a comparison, and the passage says some grains last decades, not that all do.

items.stem:
This year’s seed swap at the Hollow Creek grange drew three hundred people, forty kinds of tomato, and one long argument about whether the lumpy purple one qualifies as food. The argument was settled by a grandmother with a paring knife and a salt shaker, who declared it excellent and took home a dozen seeds. Organizers apologize for the shortage of folding chairs and promise to bring more, though nobody believes them.

Which word best describes the tone of the passage?
options: Gravely and sternly serious
Bitterly and openly critical
Lightly humorous
Detached and technical
items.explanation: The lumpy purple tomato argument, the grandmother with a salt shaker and the promise nobody believes all invite a smile, which gives a lightly humorous tone. Gravely and sternly serious ignores the jokes. Bitter criticism is absent, since the organizers are only teased, and a technical tone would avoid personal details such as these.

items.stem:
Of the 120 jars retested this year, 104 remained viable, meaning that most of their seeds could still sprout. Eleven jars showed declining rates and were scheduled for regrowing. Five jars, all of an old flax variety, failed completely, and the bank has asked three growers whether any seed of the variety survives in their own collections.

As used in the passage, the word viable most nearly means which of the following?
options: popular among growers
capable of sprouting
inexpensive to store
safe to eat
items.explanation: The passage defines the word itself: viable jars are those whose seeds could still sprout. Popular among growers and inexpensive to store describe unrelated qualities, and safe to eat is a different concern altogether, since the retest counts sprouting and says nothing about food safety.

items.stem:
Text 1: I started saving bean seeds because my aunt’s variety was vanishing. I never thought of it as science, only as keeping something alive. Text 2: Home savers keep varieties adapted to local soil. Without them, a bank would hold only seeds collected a century ago, frozen and unchanged by new weather.

Which statement best describes the relationship between the two texts?
options: Text 2 explains why the kind of saving described in Text 1 has wider value
Text 2 disputes that home saving keeps any bean variety alive for many years
Both texts argue that banks should replace home gardens
Text 1 gives a scientific method that Text 2 repeats
items.explanation: Text 1 gives a personal reason for saving beans, and Text 2 shows that such home saving keeps varieties adapted to changing conditions, which is its wider value. Text 2 supports home saving rather than disputing it. Neither text wants banks to replace gardens, and Text 1 says it was not science at all.

items.stem:
Notice to contractors: Orders placed before 10 a.m. are loaded the same day. Pressure-treated lumber must be stacked flat and strapped when you take it, since a single bowed board can ruin a whole load of decking. Our kiln-dried framing stock stays under cover in Shed Two; boards left outside overnight take on moisture, and we cannot guarantee their grade. Pickup staff will gladly help you load, but please bring your own straps.

What can be inferred about boards left outside overnight?
options: They are priced lower than the boards that are kept under cover in Shed Two
Contractors are always required to reject them
They receive an extra treatment during the night
Their quality may change, so the yard will not vouch for them
items.explanation: The notice says outdoor boards take on moisture and that the yard cannot guarantee their grade, so their quality may change and the yard will not vouch for them. No price cut is mentioned, no rule forces contractors to reject them, and nothing suggests the yard treats them at night.

items.stem:
Walter Ibeh has stacked lumber at Brannock Yard for thirty-one years, and he can identify most boards without glancing at the stamp. Cedar, he says, smells like a pencil box, and oak like a cellar. Customers sometimes test him by holding a board behind their backs, and he has never named the wrong wood. The younger staff keep a notebook of his rules, though he warns that a notebook is no substitute for handling the wood.

Why does the author include the detail about customers holding boards behind their backs?
options: To show the depth of Walter’s skill
To suggest that Walter dislikes his customers
To explain how lumber is officially graded
To prove that stamps on boards are unreliable
items.explanation: The testing game ends with Walter never naming the wrong wood, which demonstrates how thoroughly he knows wood. Nothing shows he dislikes customers, since he plays along. Grading is not explained, and the passage only says he can identify boards without a stamp, not that stamps are wrong.

items.stem:
Green lumber is full of water, and if it dries unevenly, it warps. Kiln drying avoids this by heating stacks of boards in a chamber where humidity is lowered in small steps over several days. Spacers between the layers let warm air pass through every board. The slow schedule matters: if the kiln is too hot or too dry at first, the surface shrinks before the core, and the board cups or splits.

According to the passage, what causes a board to cup or split in the kiln?
options: The spacers block warm air from passing between the layers of boards in the stack
The surface shrinks before the core when drying starts too harshly
Humidity is lowered in many small steps
Water is added to the core during drying
items.explanation: The passage says that when the kiln is too hot or too dry at first, the surface shrinks before the core and the board cups or splits. Spacers are there to let air through, not block it. Lowering humidity in small steps is the protective schedule, and no water is added to the core.

items.stem:
Brannock Yard price list, spring: Pine two-by-fours cost less than cedar of the same size, and premium grade costs about a fifth more than standard grade. Knots are the main difference: standard boards carry several, while premium boards carry few and small ones. Delivery is free within five miles for orders above $300, and otherwise costs a flat $25.

A customer within five miles orders $280 of pine. What will delivery cost?
options: Nothing, because the customer lives within five miles of the yard’s front gate
A fifth more than the order total, as with premium grade
A flat fee, because the order is under the free-delivery minimum
Nothing, because pine is the cheaper wood
items.explanation: Free delivery requires an order above $300, and $280 falls short, so the flat $25 fee applies even within five miles. Distance alone does not earn free delivery. The fifth more applies to premium boards, not delivery, and the wood type does not change the delivery rule.

items.stem:
To the Editor: The yard on Brannock Road is more than a place to buy boards. When the flood took the Dennis family’s porch, the manager sent a truckload of lumber on credit and asked for nothing in writing. That kind of trust cannot be stacked on a shelf, and it is why I drive past two bigger stores to shop there.

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the letter?
options: Bigger stores in the region treat their customers unfairly and ignore their needs
A yard’s generosity during a crisis can earn a customer’s lasting loyalty
Lumber costs less when it is bought on credit
Floods are common near Brannock Road
items.explanation: The writer describes the manager lending lumber on trust after a flood and says that trust is why the writer passes two bigger stores, so generosity earning loyalty is the central idea. The letter does not accuse larger stores of unfairness, make claims about credit prices, or say how often floods occur.

items.stem:
The Maple Court Crossword Club meets every Wednesday at 6:30 p.m. in the community room. The first half hour is open solving with shared pencils, followed by a themed puzzle on the projector at 7:00. Newcomers may borrow a clipboard and a starter grid with easier clues. On the last Wednesday of each month, members bring snacks and swap original puzzles they have written themselves.

According to the schedule, what happens on the last Wednesday of each month?
options: A themed puzzle is shown on the projector
Newcomers receive starter grids
Open solving is skipped
Members swap puzzles they have written
items.explanation: The schedule says that on the last Wednesday members bring snacks and swap original puzzles they have written. The projector puzzle and the starter grids are part of every meeting, and the passage never says open solving is skipped on that night. The detail about monthly swapping is stated once and matches only the last Wednesday.

items.stem:
Building a crossword begins with the longest entries, because they are hardest to place. A constructor chooses a theme, writes three or four long answers that share it, and sets them in symmetrical rows. Shorter words are then fitted into the gaps, and awkward letter clusters are replaced until every crossing makes a real word. Only after the grid is filled does the constructor write the clues.

According to the passage, why does a constructor place the long entries first?
options: They are the easiest to rewrite later
They carry the clues for the shorter words
They are the hardest to fit into the grid
Symmetry cannot be achieved with short words
items.explanation: The first sentence gives the reason directly: the long entries are placed first because they are hardest to place. The passage says shorter words fill the gaps afterward, which makes the long ones the less flexible part. It does not say they hold clues, and the passage never claims short words cannot be symmetrical.

items.stem:
Reviewer’s note: The collection promises fiendish puzzles, and for the first ten pages it delivers. After that, the fiendishness thins into trivia: three clues in a row ask for the name of a river. The grids are cleanly built and the print is large, which counts for something. But a book that advertises cleverness should offer more than rivers, and I closed it feeling that I had been promised a feast and handed a snack.

Which phrase best describes the reviewer’s tone?
options: Mildly disappointed
Enthusiastically delighted
Furious and scornful
Indifferent and bored
items.explanation: The reviewer praises the clean grids and large print but regrets that the cleverness fades, and ends with a feast and snack comparison, which shows mild disappointment. Delight contradicts the complaint. Fury is too strong for the measured language, and indifference would not produce such specific regret.

items.stem:
Odalys Prenn solves the Thursday puzzle in pen, on the bus, in eleven minutes, and then, to the irritation of her seatmates, sighs. ‘Too easy,’ she says. Last winter, though, one clue stumped her for three days. She asked everyone she met, scribbled it on napkins, and finally dreamed the answer. When she told the club, she was more cheerful than anyone had ever seen her.

What can be inferred about why Odalys was so cheerful?
options: She had finally stopped solving the Thursday puzzle in pen during her bus rides
Her seatmates had at last praised her
Solving a hard clue gave her more satisfaction than the easy puzzles
She learned the clue had been misprinted
items.explanation: She finds the usual puzzle too easy and sighs, yet a clue that stumped her for three days brings great cheer when she cracks it, so a real challenge satisfied her most. Nothing connects her mood to the pen, praise from seatmates, or a misprint, which the passage never mentions.

items.stem:
In a cryptic crossword, every clue holds two puzzles: a definition and a piece of wordplay that builds the same answer. Solvers new to the form often feel misled, because the surface of a clue usually describes something unrelated to the answer. With practice, the apparent nonsense starts to resolve into patterns, such as anagram signals or hidden words.

As used in the passage, the word surface most nearly means which of the following?
options: the flat upper face of a kitchen table
the outward reading of the clue
an uncovered area
a smooth finish
items.explanation: The passage says the surface of a clue describes something unrelated to the answer, which means what the clue seems to say on first reading. The top of a table and an uncovered area are physical meanings with no link to words, and a smooth finish describes texture rather than meaning.

items.stem:
The Calder Hill Youth Orchestra will perform its spring concert on April 12 at Alvarez Hall, with 64 players aged nine to eighteen. The program pairs a lively dance suite with a slow movement for strings, and a seventeen-year-old cellist will play the solo in the final piece. Tickets cost $6 for adults, and children under twelve enter free. Proceeds buy replacement strings and rental instruments for students who cannot afford their own.

What is the main idea of the news brief?
options: A low-cost spring concert will also support the orchestra’s players
A seventeen-year-old cellist is leaving the orchestra to study music abroad
Children under twelve will perform the slow movement
Alvarez Hall is being renovated for the month of April
items.explanation: The brief announces the April 12 concert, its modest ticket prices, and the use of proceeds for strings and rental instruments, so a low-cost concert that supports players is the main idea. The cellist only plays a solo, children under twelve are admitted free rather than performing, and the hall is never described as under renovation.

items.stem:
Rehearsal notes, March 3. The violins rushed again in bars 40 to 56. Mr. Dube tried a new method: instead of counting aloud, he had the cellos play a steady pulse while the violins whispered their part. The rushing stopped almost immediately. He told them afterward, ‘You were not hurrying because you were nervous. You were hurrying because you could not hear each other.’

What does the director’s remark suggest caused the rushing?
options: The violinists were nervous about playing in front of the concert audience
The violinists had not practiced at home
The cellos were playing too softly throughout
The players had trouble hearing one another’s parts
items.explanation: Mr. Dube rules out nervousness and says the violins hurried because they could not hear each other, a claim supported by the quick fix of a steady cello pulse. Nervousness is the cause he rejects. Home practice is never mentioned, and the cellos were not blamed, since their steady pulse solved the problem.

items.stem:
Before every rehearsal, the oboe plays a single note, and the whole orchestra tunes to it. The oboe is chosen because its pitch is steady and cuts clearly through the sound of the others, even from the back of the stage. Players adjust their instruments in small amounts until their sound matches the oboe’s, a step that takes less than a minute but spares the audience a muddy performance.

As used in the passage, the word pitch most nearly means which of the following?
options: how high or low a note sounds
a presentation made to sell something
the slope of a roof
a throw aimed at a catcher
items.explanation: The sentence describes a note that is steady and that the other instruments match, so pitch means how high or low it sounds. A sales presentation, a roof slope and a throw are all real meanings of the word, but none of them can describe the quality of an oboe’s note that players tune toward.

items.stem:
Dear Mr. Dube, My son Kofi came home from his first rehearsal talking about nothing else. He has never liked practicing anything, yet last night I found him in the garage, bow in hand, playing the same four bars until they sounded right. I do not know what you said to him, but thank you. I only ask that you keep reminding him that the sloppy bars are part of the process.

Which statement best describes the writer’s attitude toward Mr. Dube?
options: Doubtful about his teaching methods
Curious about his career before the orchestra
Grateful for his positive influence
Annoyed by the length of the rehearsals
items.explanation: The writer thanks Mr. Dube and credits him, without knowing how, for Kofi’s new interest in practicing, which shows gratitude. The request to keep reminding Kofi about sloppy bars is support, not doubt. The letter never asks about his career and does not complain about rehearsal length.

items.stem:
Rehearsal schedule: Strings meet Mondays from 4:00 to 5:30; winds and brass meet Tuesdays from 4:00 to 5:30; the full orchestra meets Saturdays from 10:00 to noon. The week of the concert, the full orchestra also meets Thursday evening. Absences must be reported to the librarian by Friday noon of the week before.

A bassoonist wants to attend every rehearsal in a normal week. On which days should she plan to be there?
options: Monday and Saturday
Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday
Monday, Tuesday and Saturday
Tuesday and Saturday
items.explanation: The bassoon is a wind instrument, so she attends the Tuesday winds session and the Saturday full rehearsal. Monday is for strings. The Thursday evening meeting happens only during concert week, so it is not part of a normal week, and adding Monday would put her in a string rehearsal.

items.stem:
Making a container candle begins with melting wax flakes in a pot set inside a larger pot of simmering water, which prevents scorching. Once the wax reaches about 170 degrees, the maker stirs in fragrance oil, then lets it cool to around 140 before pouring. Pouring too hot causes the wax to shrink away from the glass as it hardens, leaving gaps along the sides.

According to the passage, what happens if wax is poured while too hot?
options: It scorches in the larger pot
It pulls away from the glass as it hardens
The fragrance grows noticeably stronger as the wax cools
The wick sinks into the wax
items.explanation: The passage states that pouring too hot makes the wax shrink away from the glass as it hardens, leaving gaps. Scorching is prevented by the double pot earlier in the process, not by the pouring temperature. Fragrance strength and a sinking wick are never connected to heat in the text.

items.stem:
Ilse Marchetti began pouring candles in a rented garage with one pot and a borrowed thermometer. Now her workshop on Quill Street employs six people, most of them former students from her weekend classes. She still pours the first batch of every new scent herself, because, she says, ‘a scent has to survive my own impatience before it earns a label.’ Her best seller is a plain beeswax pillar that has no scent at all.

Which detail best supports the idea that Ilse remains closely involved in production?
options: She pours the first batch of every new scent herself
Her workshop employs six people, most of them former students
She began in a rented garage
Her best seller is an unscented pillar
items.explanation: Pouring every first batch herself is direct evidence that she is still hands-on with production. The staff of six shows the business has grown and could suggest she has delegated. The garage start is history, and the unscented best seller concerns sales, not her own involvement.

items.stem:
I signed up for the candle workshop expecting to sit politely and sniff things. Instead, I spilled lavender wax on my sleeve, nearly poured a candle with no wick, and finished with a lopsided jar that leans like a tired tree. I adore it. The instructor, Priyanka, laughed at every disaster with me, never at me, and sent us home with a list of fixes. I have already signed up for the next class.

Which phrase best describes the tone of the passage?
options: Resentful and defensive
Formal and reserved
Fearful and uncertain
Cheerful and self-mocking
items.explanation: The writer jokes about the spilled wax and the jar that leans like a tired tree, then says she adores it and has signed up again, which is cheerful and self-mocking. Resentment would not lead to a second class. The playful comparisons are not formal, and no fear remains after the laughter.

items.stem:
Workshop safety notice: Never leave melting wax unattended, and never use water to put out a wax fire; cover the pot with a lid and turn off the burner instead. Keep fragrance oils away from the stove, because they can ignite. Long hair should be tied back, and aprons are provided at the door. Questions about the rules should be raised before the session begins, not during pouring.

The author most likely wrote the notice for which purpose?
options: To advertise an upcoming candle class held at the workshop
To give participants rules for working safely
To describe the history of candle making
To persuade readers to buy fragrance oils
items.explanation: Each sentence is a rule or instruction about fire, oils, hair or aprons, so the aim is to help participants work safely. Nothing advertises a class, and no history of candles appears. Fragrance oils are mentioned only as a hazard to keep away from the stove, not as something to sell.

items.stem:
Text 1: Scented candles fill a room within minutes and make a space feel finished. For gifts, nothing beats a jar with a name like Cedar Rain. Text 2: Strong fragrance bothers many people, and it can mask the clean glow that makes a candle worth lighting. A plain beeswax pillar offers warmth without asking anything of the nose.

What do the two texts disagree about?
options: Whether candles make suitable gifts
Whether wax can be melted safely
Whether fragrance improves a candle
Whether beeswax is a kind of wax
items.explanation: Text 1 praises scent for filling a room, while Text 2 says fragrance bothers people and hides the glow, so they disagree about whether fragrance improves a candle. Gifts are mentioned only in Text 1. Neither text discusses melting safety, and calling beeswax a wax is simply assumed by both.

items.stem:
The Marlow Heights weather station recorded 31 millimeters of rain in the first week of October, nearly triple the normal total. Most of it fell on a single night, when a slow storm stalled over the valley. Streams rose by half a meter, and two footbridges were closed for inspection. Forecasters say the soil is now saturated, so even modest rain this month could cause local flooding.

Why do forecasters warn that modest rain could now cause flooding?
options: The ground can no longer absorb much more water
The two footbridges have been permanently removed
Another slow storm is certain to stall over the valley
The streams were completely dry before the storm
items.explanation: The report says the soil is saturated, so the ground can take in little more water and even modest rain may run off and flood. The footbridges were only closed for inspection. A second storm is not predicted as certain, and the streams rose by half a meter, which shows they held water.

items.stem:
The Eastgate Bike Co-op needs you. Every Saturday, volunteers repair about thirty donated bicycles, and every Saturday we turn away families because there are not enough mechanics. You do not need experience; we will teach you to true a wheel and set a brake. Come for an hour, bring gloves if you have them, and leave knowing you gave a child a way to ride to school.

What is the main purpose of this notice?
options: To explain to new mechanics how brakes are adjusted on bikes
To persuade readers to join the repair effort as volunteers
To report how many bikes were sold last year
To warn families about unsafe bicycles
items.explanation: The notice opens with ‘needs you,’ describes a shortage of mechanics, and ends by inviting readers to give an hour, so it aims to persuade people to volunteer. Brake training is only an offer. No sales figures appear, and the bikes are donated and repaired, not warned against.

items.stem:
A wobbling wheel can usually be fixed by adjusting its spokes. The mechanic spins the wheel in a stand and watches where the rim brushes against a small pointer. Tightening the spokes on the opposite side pulls the rim back toward the center. This careful adjustment, called truing, is done in quarter-turns, because a full turn on one spoke can overcorrect and create a new wobble elsewhere.

As used in the passage, the word overcorrect most nearly means which of the following?
options: repair a part twice
inspect a part closely
adjust by more than is needed
measure a part in advance
items.explanation: The passage explains that a full turn on one spoke can create a new wobble, which means the adjustment goes further than needed, so overcorrect means adjust too far. Repairing twice, inspecting closely and measuring in advance each describe a different action and do not explain why a new wobble appears.

items.stem:
A reflector telescope and a refractor both gather light, but they do it differently. A refractor uses a glass lens at the front, so light passes through and bends toward a focus. A reflector uses a curved mirror at the back, so light bounces to a focus near the front. Refractors tend to be narrow and long, while reflectors can be built wider and cheaper, which is why many amateur astronomers prefer them for faint objects.

How is the passage mainly organized?
options: By listing events in time order
By describing a problem and its cure
By tracing a single cause through its long chain of effects
By contrasting two devices that serve the same purpose
items.explanation: The passage opens by saying the two telescopes gather light differently, then describes each design and ends with their trade-offs, which is a contrast. No events are placed in time order. No problem and fix are given, and no single cause is followed through a chain of effects.

items.stem:
Dear neighbors, The plot rental fee at the Cedar Lot garden will rise from $18 to $24 next season. The increase is not meant to make money; the water bill has doubled since the hose lines were repaired, and the shed roof needs replacing. Gardeners who cannot afford the new fee may trade two hours of work per month for a full discount. Please contact the board before February 15.

Which detail from the letter best explains why the fee is increasing?
options: Gardeners may trade two work hours each month for a full discount
The water bill has doubled and the shed roof needs replacing
The board must be contacted before February 15
The fee was $18 during the previous season
items.explanation: The letter gives its reason in the second sentence: the water bill has doubled and the shed roof needs replacing. The work trade is an option for those who cannot pay, the deadline concerns contacting the board, and the old fee only states the starting point, not why it rises.

items.stem:
Field notes, Gull Point, Day 4. High tide at 5:12 a.m. covered the lower rocks completely, and the terns that nest there moved to the grass above. By noon, the water had dropped nearly two meters and the terns returned, picking through the weed for small crabs. Their routine follows the water so closely that I can nearly set my watch by it.

What can be inferred about the terns’ behavior?
options: They leave Gull Point for good whenever the tide climbs over the rocks
They feed only on the grass above the rocks
They are disturbed by the observer’s watch
Their activity is tied to the rising and falling tide
items.explanation: The terns leave the covered rocks at high tide and return when the water drops, and the writer says their routine follows the water, so their activity tracks the tide. They come back, so they do not leave for good. They feed on crabs among weed, and the watch is only a figure of speech.

items.stem:
To keep the ice smooth, the Orrin Park rink uses a resurfacing machine that shaves a thin layer from the surface, collects the snow, and lays down a film of warm water. The warm water settles into the cut grooves and then freezes flat. If the water were cold, it would freeze in ridges instead. That is why skaters often see a shimmering wet sheet for a few moments before it hardens.

Why does the machine lay down warm water instead of cold water?
options: Cold water would melt the ice entirely and make the surface unsafe
Warm water removes the snow from the surface
Warm water settles into grooves before it freezes flat
Skaters prefer a wet surface to a dry one
items.explanation: The passage says warm water settles into the cut grooves and freezes flat, while cold water would freeze in ridges. Cold water melting the ice is never claimed. The machine collects snow separately by shaving, and skaters merely notice the wet sheet; their preference is not mentioned.

items.stem:
Westfield Market: Produce stalls open at 8:00 a.m. and close at 1:00 p.m. Baked goods usually sell out by 11:00, so regular shoppers arrive early. Parking is free in the east lot but limited; the west lot charges $3 and has more spaces. A shuttle runs from the library every twenty minutes.

A shopper wants fresh bread and prefers a lot with plenty of spaces. Which plan fits the information?
options: Arrive before 11:00 and park in the west lot
Arrive at noon and park in the east lot
Arrive after 11:00 and park in the west lot to avoid the fee
Arrive at 1:00 and take the shuttle from the library
items.explanation: Bread usually sells out by 11:00, so the shopper must arrive earlier, and the west lot is the one with more spaces. Noon is too late for bread, and the east lot is limited. The west lot charges a fee, so it cannot avoid one, and arriving at 1:00 misses the baked goods.

items.stem:
Ansel Kobe keeps nine hives behind the old schoolhouse. He moves slowly, speaks softly, and wears a veil only when the bees are agitated. ‘They sense your mood,’ he says, ‘so do not carry your worries into the hive.’ Neighbors who once complained about the buzzing now line up each fall for jars of his honey, which tastes faintly of clover.

As used in the passage, the word agitated most nearly means which of the following?
options: deeply asleep
heavily loaded
newly hatched
stirred up and restless
items.explanation: Ansel wears a veil only when the bees are agitated and says they sense a person’s mood, so agitated describes bees that are stirred up and restless. Deeply asleep would make a veil unnecessary. Heavily loaded and newly hatched describe other conditions and do not explain why protection would be needed.

items.stem:
The new exhibit at the Harrow Museum, A Century of Telephones, promises a tour of invention but delivers a closet. Eleven phones sit behind glass with labels so brief they barely qualify as explanation. One label reads only ‘Black phone, 1930s.’ The staff are kind and the building is lovely, but visitors who hoped to understand how these machines changed daily life will leave with nothing but a date.

Which sentence best supports the claim that the exhibit lacks explanation?
options: The staff are kind and the building is lovely.
The exhibit promises a tour of invention.
One label reads only ‘Black phone, 1930s.’
The museum is named after a town called Harrow.
items.explanation: A label that gives only a color and a decade is direct evidence of missing explanation. The kindness of the staff and the lovely building are compliments that do not address labels. The promise of a tour describes what the exhibit advertises, and the museum’s name has no bearing on the question.

items.stem:
Text 1: Barges move slowly, but a single horse could once pull a load that would take ten wagons. That efficiency kept canals busy for decades. Text 2: Railways ended the canal age. A train covered in an afternoon what a barge covered in three days, and merchants chose speed.

Which statement best describes how the two texts treat canals?
options: Both texts argue that barges were faster than trains
Text 1 gives a strength of canals, while Text 2 gives the reason for their decline
Text 1 blames horses for the decline of canals, and Text 2 blames the merchants who shipped goods
Text 2 praises the efficiency described in Text 1
items.explanation: Text 1 credits canals with moving heavy loads cheaply, and Text 2 says trains replaced them because merchants wanted speed. Neither claims barges were faster, since both admit barges were slow. Text 1 never blames horses for any decline, and Text 2 does not praise canal efficiency.

items.stem:
A wick that is too thin cannot melt wax across the full width of a candle, so the flame sinks into a narrow tunnel and drowns. A wick that is too thick burns a large flame that makes sooty smoke and leaves soft wax pools. Choosing a wick therefore means matching its width to the jar’s diameter: the wider the jar, the thicker the wick.

According to the passage, what results from a wick that is too thin?
options: The flame sinks into a narrow tunnel in the wax
The candle burns with a large sooty flame
The wax melts too quickly across the jar
The wick grows thicker as it burns
items.explanation: A thin wick cannot melt the full width of the wax, so the flame sinks into a narrow tunnel and drowns. The large sooty flame is the result of a wick that is too thick. Wax melting too fast across the jar is the opposite of the problem, and wicks do not thicken as they burn.

items.stem:
Retired engineer Halvard Pike arrives at the canal lock each morning with a thermos and a folding stool, though no one has asked him to supervise. He never lifts a tool. Instead, he watches the masons set each block and now and then raises one finger. The masons, without comment, lift the block, check it with a level, and set it again. ‘He has been right every time,’ says the foreman.

What can be inferred about Halvard’s role at the lock?
options: He is the foreman in charge of hiring and directing the masons
He disapproves of the masons’ work
He is an informal advisor whose judgment the masons trust
He is waiting for his own turn to lay blocks
items.explanation: The masons reset a block each time he raises a finger, and the foreman says he has been right every time, so he acts as an unofficial advisor they trust. The foreman is a separate person. His signal leads to improvement, not disapproval, and he never lifts a tool or waits for a turn.

items.stem:
Builders prefer seasoned lumber for furniture, because a board that has been dried slowly for a year or more moves very little once it is cut and joined. Fresh lumber, still wet, shrinks as it dries and can pull joints apart within a few weeks. The extra cost of seasoned wood is therefore easily repaid in repairs avoided.

As used in the passage, the word seasoned most nearly means which of the following?
options: flavored with spices
experienced and skilled
painted for protection
dried gradually until stable
items.explanation: The passage defines seasoned wood as a board dried slowly for a year or more so that it moves very little. Flavored with spices applies to food, experienced and skilled describes a person, and painted for protection names a coating that the passage never mentions.

items.stem:
Ten years ago the Calder Hill Youth Orchestra had nine members, one borrowed piano, and a rehearsal room that flooded in March. Today it has sixty-four players, a donated hall, and a waiting list. Founder Ines Varga credits the growth to a simple rule: any child who wants to play will be given an instrument and a seat. ‘We did not recruit,’ she says. ‘We kept the door open, and word traveled.’

Which statement best expresses the central idea of the passage?
options: Flooded rehearsal rooms are a common problem for youth orchestras everywhere
An open-door policy helped a small orchestra grow into a large one
A waiting list shows that the hall is too small
Recruiting is the only way to grow an orchestra
items.explanation: The founder credits the growth from nine members to sixty-four to the rule that any child who wants to play gets an instrument and a seat, so the open door is the central idea. The flood is only part of the early story. The waiting list is not linked to hall size, and she says they did not recruit.
